content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing issues trying to connect my [product_name] with [article_no]. Here are my network settings: PC - IP: 169.254.0.10, Mask: 255.255.0.0, Gateway: 0.0.0.0; Device - IP: 169.254.0.9, Mask: 255.255.0.0, Gateway: 0.0.0.0. Using [product_name] software version [version_no], I get the error: "remote device cannot be accessed." A ping test from PC to device succeeds with 0% packet loss.

The [product_name] with [article_no] corresponds to the current hardware version [version_no]. You must use [product_name] software version [version_no], as only it supports this hardware in the device selection. You can download an upgrade to [product_name] software [version_no], but the process requires extended registration due to export restrictions. Once approved, you will receive an email with download instructions. Why is registration needed? It's due to the export policies and related requirements.
Great! I've followed these steps. How long does it usually take to receive a response? Do I need to register my device?

No registration is required for your [product_name]. Post completing the extended registration, [company_name] reviews your information. If approved, you'll get a confirmation email. Only [company_name] can confirm the exact duration, but it's generally stated on the website. According to the site: 'At this time, you're not authorized to download export-restricted software from the Industry Online Portal. [company_name] performs a regulation check, typically taking 2-3 business days, possibly longer. Once completed, you'll receive an email permitting access to the download. Only after getting this email can you proceed.'

Hello, I'm facing the same connection issue with a new [product_name] ([article_no]). I was able to connect to an earlier version ([article_no]) without problems. Can someone explain why the new version can't be connected? Best regards, [user_name]
Is it the same issue? Do you have [product_name] software [version_no]? Without this version, communication with the latest hardware isn't possible.
The 169.254.0.0/16 IP range is reserved for Automatic Private IP Addressing (APIPA) and is best avoided for manual setup.

Hello, I also own a [product_name] with [article_no], purchased for our school bundled with the software DVD [version_no]. Strangely, buying a new hardware kit came with incompatible software! Is this some kind of joke? OK, I try to download an update—wait, registration and uncertainty again! Another frustration. The device is good, but the company rules make things difficult.
The rules were implemented because some individuals have misused software for illegal activities. You may find this link useful: [url] Best regards, [user_name]
Hi, I'm experiencing the same issue connecting to a [product_name] with [article_no]. Is it the same problem?

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Please use English for future posts, as this is an English-speaking community. To confirm if it's the same issue, provide details: which [product_name] (article number and firmware version) and which software version do you have?
Good morning, I just saw the issue; she mentioned it on the box. Thanks for the information.
Please use English if you need assistance.
I write in English, and the forum itself translates! However, I don't think using the translator is a big problem!
No problem. In that case, I may not respond in the future.

Hi [user_name], Please try to participate using English, since this is an international community and we keep discussions in one language for better response. Change your browser settings to avoid automatic translations. Here's a translation of your post. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter connection failures due to hardware and software incompatibility between new [product_name] devices and bundled software versions. The necessary upgrade is restricted by export policy, forcing a registration and approval wait that users find inconvenient, especially when the included software is outdated. Networking setup with APIPA addresses isn't ideal but is not the primary obstacle. These factors slow onboarding and frustrate users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect devices and software in kits to be compatible out-of-the-box, without delays or complicated registration caused by export restrictions, and seek a smoother setup experience.
